---
title: "Interval overlap across 435 pairs"
subtitle: "1.12 · the posterior intervals of a simulated league and the directions they hide, after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024)"
description: "Comparison of marginal interval overlap and direction probabilities in a thirty-unit simulation."
---

The thirty units of the simulated league yield 435 unordered pairs. Their posterior intervals are calculated under
the normal model used in [normal–normal posterior shrinkage](shrinkage.qmd). For each selected pair, the display gives the
interval overlap and the posterior probability that the first unit has the larger true value. The table distinguishes
non-overlapping intervals from overlapping intervals with, or without, a direction probability above .90. This
classification quantifies the extent to which interval overlap coexists with relatively high posterior support for
one direction. It also permits comparisons across interval levels and prior standard deviations.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Overlap, highest probability.** 399 of the 435 pairs have overlapping 90% intervals, and 88 of them still have one
  direction above .90. The highest is .988, for U13 above U05, whose intervals overlap by .005: no overlapping pair is
  above .99.
- **U06 and U20.** These intervals do not overlap (.002 lies between them), and U06 is the higher with probability
  .988, the same to three decimals as the overlapping pair above: the two comparisons have similar posterior support despite different overlap classifications.
- **U04 and U18.** A wide overlap, .107, and still U04 is the higher with probability .904: U18's narrow interval ends
  at −.105, below U04's posterior mean, −.014.
- **95% intervals.** Wider intervals overlap more often, in 413 pairs, and 102 of these have one direction above .90.
  The highest is now .997, for U03 above U15.
- **Prior SD .05.** A narrow prior pulls every posterior mean toward zero: 427 pairs overlap, only 58 of them with one
  direction above .90.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
For two independent normal posteriors, whatever their SDs, the more likely direction has a probability above .950 when
their 90% intervals do not overlap. When they overlap, it is at most .990, the value for equal SDs and intervals that
just touch (.975 and .997 for 95% intervals). Kline, Rose and Walters (2024, section IV.C) draw a credible interval
beside each name, but they grade the names from pairwise posterior probabilities.
:::

Standalone: [embed/overlap-in-the-league.html](../../embed/overlap-in-the-league.html), for example `?pair=U05-U13`
(U05 first: the card gives .012) or `?preset=league-95&theme=dark`.
